recorded-direction.text: The decisions favor project-level contracts, roots for every block, checkpoint-bound queries, raw transaction reconstruction and optional application proof services. The diagram separates design direction, reviewed models and production implementation.

named-deployment-roles.text: Anchors and ledgers run nodes. Anchors serve signed roots; ledgers serve data and proofs. Applications serve application proofs. Terminals consume all three, verify them and build transactions or drive real-world effects. The names describe roles rather than a fixed deployment count.

words-that-constrain-the-design.text: The project separates immutable hashed content from chain indexes. Anchors publish roots for every block. Proof-bearing answers bind to an externally supplied root; later discussion clarified that reconstruction transactions may arrive without individual proofs.

Ledger proofs are checked off-chain and are not placed in transaction redeemers. Application proofs are placed in redeemers. Cardano checks actual ledger validity, and application validators check the application proofs.

what-remains-unproved.text: Commitment coverage, complete-set proofs, archive sufficiency, publisher policy and session rollback behavior are still unresolved. Application verification must bind the intended identity and state.

evidence-available-today.text: MPFS already verifies reconstructed facts against an anchored state root. The inspected Koios and Blockfrost interfaces do not promise the required shared chain-point sessions. Related root-signing work is not evidence that the whole publication protocol exists.
